call_sites: reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:33-47 (crew_station CLI verb, imported by reckon/cli.py:226 onward so the command registers on the crew group)

findings.summary: node_lock duplicates the single-owner-with-holder-identity capability the repository already owns in reckon/crew/host_lease.py:26 (HostLease.claim/holder, which records host and pid and names the holder) and in the fleet supervisor's lifetime service lock probed by reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:720; it neither wraps nor extends either owner, and the overlap should be folded onto one when the supervisor launch named in plan section 7 lands. It is non-blocking because the plan fixes a lock under the node-local runtime root, neither owner exposes that guarantee as a callable, and the repository repeats flock inline in several modules.

Plan section 7 also states the station is the only process that reloads onto new code from a reload image under the runtime root and is started by the crew host or the fleet supervisor; the landed change implements neither, so section 7 is not complete with this node alone even though the node goal does not name reload. It is recorded in the manifest's outside_scope and is non-blocking here.

The payload assertion compares the serialized event's run_id against the row's run column, and both derive from the same event mapping passed to StationStore.record_tick, so it cannot detect a payload written from the wrong event; it does still fail if the column is null or mis-encoded, so it is weak coverage rather than a vacuous guard.

justifications.durability: Reverting the baseline seeding at reckon/crew/station.py:99 and the offset persistence would redden tests/test_one_station_per_node_runs_the_tick.py:161 and :236, and the declared lock mutation was run red in station-lock-negative.log, which fails at line 122 with EXIT=1.
justifications.evidence: tests/test_one_station_per_node_runs_the_tick.py:122 asserts the second station's refusal and :161 asserts a restart re-emits nothing, both matching the done_when; the manifest's station-committed-head.log records 5 passed with EXIT=0.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/station.py follows the module idiom beside station_store.py, reuses recovery/ticker rather than re-deriving them, uses a lazy import for the adoption call, and introduces no plan label or version name.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/station.py:68 tick() ingests, calls store.classify_tick, writes folded transitions with audience and duty via store.record_tick, and moves the heartbeat, and :29 node_lock holds one runtime-root lock for the process lifetime.
justifications.reuse: The fold reuses recovery.fleet_transitions and recovery._watch_transition and extends StationStore in place, but reckon/crew/station.py:29 node_lock writes its own holder record where reckon/crew/host_lease.py:26 already owns that claim.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat across 9c689e62..723aa95d lists only the five declared paths, and the store's new payload column and pointer-row cleanup in reckon/crew/station_store.py:378 serve the same restart guarantee rather than an unrelated goal.

notes: Reviewed base 9c689e62 is an ancestor of the reviewed head; the review worktree's own HEAD (bf07b346d) is not, so the landed commits are not yet on main and were read from the object store rather than the working tree. The manifest's single importer failure test_every_module_is_reached was confirmed as scaffolding by its own traceback (git cat-file exits 128 with no .git in the extracted tree) and it is identical in both arms, so added_failure_count is 0.
